official_measurement_examples.name: HRB route separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK directs higher-risk building work to the Building Safety Regulator while non-higher-risk work can use a local authority or registered building control approver; these routes must remain distinct.

official_measurement_examples.name: Full plans versus building notice
official_measurement_examples.fact: Full plans provide a formal plan-decision route, while a building notice does not provide the same formal approval before work starts.

official_measurement_examples.name: Building notice start limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK states work can normally start 2 days after a building notice is submitted, but this is not proof the finished work complies with building regulations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Regularisation limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Retrospective regularisation is available through a local-authority building control body for qualifying work carried out after 11 November 1985 and may require alterations before certification.

official_measurement_examples.name: Competent person scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Competent-person schemes allow registered installers to self-certify specified work; scheme membership does not self-certify work outside the member's authorised scope.

official_measurement_examples.name: Approved Documents role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Documents provide guidance on ways to meet the Building Regulations; citing an Approved Document alone is not evidence that particular completed work complies.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 building-control profession updates
official_measurement_examples.fact: Registered building control approver registration guidance was updated 1 April 2026 and professional conduct rules were updated 22 May 2026; provider status must retain current registration and scope.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Building-regulations approval concerns compliance with building standards and is a separate statutory process from land-use planning permission; one must not be used as a proxy for the other.
